header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam Gomez (Redwood Sec Eng), Rebecca Lane (Avalon CISO), Tom Nguyen (Avalon Sec Eng), Sara Patel (Avalon Infra)
Meeting link: zoom.us/recap...
Recording: available
summary: Redwood reviewed pen test findings and discussed remediation priorities, vulnerability management cadence, secure SDLC practices, and evidence for SOC 2/ISO audits. Three high severity items require code/config fixes; several medium items are infra/policy changes. Agreement to share full report and schedule a remediation planning session; Redwood to provide prescriptive remediations and re-test plan.
topics: Pen test results overview; CVE/high/medium/low classification; remediation owners and timeline; patching cadence and patch management process; secure SDLC and deployment gating; RBAC/SSO/SAML posture; KMS/HSM and encryption at rest/in transit; audit logs and retention; data residency constraints; retest and verification plan; evidence for SOC 2 and ISO 27001
transcript:
00:00 Ethan Park: okay thanks everyone for joining, we'll go over the pen test results and next steps – I'm Ethan from Redwood.
00:12 Rebecca Lane: thanks Ethan, we got the high level summary yesterday, want to walk through the details esp the high ones. we have Tom and Sara on to do the deep bits.
00:25 Priya Shah: hi all, I'll run through the findings, quick note transcription might mangle some product names (redwood dedicated might show up as Redwood Dedi).
00:40 Priya Shah: Finding 1 — high severity: unauthenticated access to internal metrics endpoint via exposed debug route; details in report page 6. PoC was trivial for the tester.
01:05 Tom Nguyen: can you remind us which service that was? was that on hosted or dedicated?
01:12 Priya Shah: looks like it's in the private deployment image we used during the test — configuration gating missed the debug flag; it's more of a config hardening than a code vuln.
01:28 Liam Gomez: fyi we recommend turning off debug, restrict to loopback, and add a mutual TLS for internal endpoints — we'll put steps.
01:45 Rebecca Lane: okay that's one we can triage quickly. what about the other highs?
01:50 Priya Shah: Finding 2 — high: KMS key-policy overly permissive allowed cross-account key usage in test env; tester used a service principal to decrypt some test blobs.
02:08 Sara Patel: was that using AWS KMS or our HSM? we use both in prod, curious which one was in scope.
02:16 Priya Shah: AWS KMS for the test cluster; the issue was key policy and IAM role trust boundary. we flagged it as high because of potential data exposure.
02:30 Ethan Park: note we recommend least-privilege key policies and recommend rotating keys, plus consider HSM-backed keys for critical PII flows.
02:48 Tom Nguyen: do you have a template policy we can apply?
02:52 Priya Shah: yes we'll include a sample key policy and an example kms/iam role change in the remediation doc.
03:05 Priya Shah: Finding 3 — high: SSRF-like request to metadata service from containerized sidecar due to open redirect in internal routing.
03:18 Rebecca Lane: that's the kind of thing we cannot accept for our bank, high priority.
03:22 Priya Shah: agreed — fix is code-level plus routing rules; we've got suggested patches.
03:35 Ethan Park: overall counts: 3 high, 7 medium, 12 low-ish. we annotated with impact to data residency and to SOC 2 control mappings.
03:50 Tom Nguyen: can you expand on the secure SDLC notes you mentioned in the report?
03:56 Priya Shah: sure — we noted gaps in PR gating for critical infra changes; for example, patching cadence for base images wasn't enforced in CI. some infra images haven't been rebuilt in 90 days.
04:15 Sara Patel: our current cadence is monthly for infra patches, but app images are weekly. we missed some OS-level CVEs due to a delayed rebuild.
04:28 Liam Gomez: recommend automated base image rebuilds with image scanning in CI; set severity threshold for auto-blocking merges (e.g., CVSS >= 7).
04:42 Rebecca Lane: what's Redwood's patching cadence in managed clusters?
04:48 Ethan Park: for hosted we do regular patch windows and emergency patching for high CVEs; for dedicated/private we provide guidance and optional managed patching add-on.
04:58 Rebecca Lane: good, we need that in writing for audits.
05:05 Priya Shah: on RBAC and SSO — pen testers found a role with overly broad admin privileges in the RBAC config for the inferencing service. they could escalate to management plane in the test env.
05:24 Tom Nguyen: are we talking about console access or API keys?
05:28 Priya Shah: console/API role mappings; also SAML assertion mapping allowed an unexpected group claim.
05:36 Ethan Park: immediate mitigation: tighten role bindings, require MFA for admin roles, and run role-binding audits quarterly.
05:50 Sara Patel: for our SOC 2 scope we'll need logs for role changes and admin sessions.
05:57 Priya Shah: audit logs — the tester confirmed logs existed but retention was only 30 days in the test config; you asked for 12 months retention earlier for audits.
06:12 Rebecca Lane: yes, we need 12 months at minimum, plus S3 write-once for certain artifacts.
06:20 Priya Shah: we recommend forwarding logs to your central SIEM with immutable storage; Redwood can support log forwarding via syslog or cloud native exporters.
06:34 Liam Gomez: also enable alerting for privilege changes and anomalous token issuance.
06:41 Ethan Park: on encryption — in transit is TLS 1.2+ across the board; at rest we recommend AES-256 with KMS-managed keys. the high finding around KMS policy is configuration not crypto weakness.
06:58 Rebecca Lane: for data residency — tester accessed a staging shard in a different region; can you confirm how region isolation is enforced?
07:10 Priya Shah: region isolation is enforced by routing policies and tenancy configs; the test setup included a region that should have been out of scope, so we've flagged routing rules. we'll provide the exact config lines to fix.
07:26 Sara Patel: audit evidence for SaaS vs private deployment: we need network diagrams and flow for the infra that handles EU customer data.
07:35 Ethan Park: we'll include architecture diagrams and data flow maps with the SOC 2 artifacts.
07:42 Tom Nguyen: remediation timelines — what's realistic for high items?
07:47 Priya Shah: depending on ownership: config fixes (debug flag, KMS policy) could be 1-2 weeks; code fixes (SSRF redirect) likely 2-4 weeks; then retest window of 2-4 weeks after fixes.
08:05 Rebecca Lane: ok we'll plan sprint capacity. we have a major release mid-Nov, prefer fixes before that.
08:12 Priya Shah: on vulnerability management process — recommend integrating vuln scanning into PRs, triage board with SLA (24h for critical, 7 days for high), and monthly vulnerability reviews.
08:30 Liam Gomez: also map findings to SOC 2 CC7 controls and show evidence of remediation for compliance reviewers.
08:40 Ethan Park: for patching cadence, we advise weekly rebuilds for app images and monthly for infra, with emergency patches as needed.
08:52 Sara Patel: can Redwood run a targeted retest for the high items?
08:56 Priya Shah: yes we offer a re-test package; can coordinate after fixes and provide a condensed retest report.
09:05 Rebecca Lane: what's included in the re-test? full exploit validation or just control checks?
09:12 Priya Shah: we do verification steps for each fixed finding and attempt exploit paths when appropriate, and confirm config and policy changes. we'll scope it with you.
09:22 Ethan Park: action: Priya will send the full PDF with annotated remediation steps and sample policies.
09:29 Priya Shah: yeah I'll also include sample KMS policy, RBAC bindings, image CI pipeline snippets, and a suggested patch cadence doc.
09:40 Tom Nguyen: for SOC 2 evidence, can you provide list of logs and retention policies Redwood can produce?
09:47 Ethan Park: yes, we'll send a matrix of artifacts (logs, architecture, config snapshots, test results) mapped to SOC 2 sections.
09:55 Rebecca Lane: any blockers around encryption/HSM for our HSM-backed keys?
09:59 Priya Shah: no blockers, we support HSM integration, will outline connection and attestation steps.
10:07 Sara Patel: the pen test mentioned some flaky results in container runtime instrumentation, could that be due to sampling?
10:14 Liam Gomez: possibly, testers reported intermittent agent timeouts in heavy load; we'll look at instrumentation config and provide tuning guidance.
10:25 Rebecca Lane: great. final ask — can you supply the remediation roadmap and a proposed date for re-test?
10:33 Ethan Park: yes — we'll propose dates in the follow-up email; based on your timeline, target re-test in early December.
10:40 Priya Shah: ok I'll share the remediation matrix by Friday 2025-11-07.
10:45 Rebecca Lane: thanks everyone, that works.
10:48 Ethan Park: recap of next steps — send report, SOC 2 docs, schedule planning call. thanks all.
10:55 Meeting Ended
notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-attributions and colloquial speech; references to 'Redwood Dedi' and product names may be transcribed inconsistently. Report PDF referenced as 'pen_test_report_avalon_2025-11.pdf'.
